units.translation: around which a tower has been driven
Thus Turnebus for περεβάλοντο [they threw around themselves].
He changed the course of the strait, and having cast around it many a fetter of hammered bonds, he accomplished a long journey.
having thrown such a yoke around Troy
I will lay the corpse, having cast around it a swift-footed bronze fetter.
the gods cast around him a winged body
as many as cast a band around their garments

these are the two outlines of the feet
see me, the suppliant, the fugitive, running around
the encircling vessel has been dashed to the ground, of the hollow-bellied circle
the wrathful curses of Oedipus, the mind-destroying
to blame those beneath the earth wrathfully
But you, stand around this altar and the flame of the fire in a circle

where he used the feminine ending, so that three words ending in -os would not follow one another. Δήλοιο περικλύστης [of sea-washed Delos] is in the Homeric Hymn to Apollo 181.
and the islands that lie along the sea-washed headland

who dwell around the ancient stream of Erasinus

The reading of this passage is uncertain, in which περιοργώς [vehemently] inserted after ὀργᾷ [he is eager] gives offense, for which the scholiast records a different reading, αὐδᾷ [he speaks]. Moreover, in M the accent is περιόργως [vehemently] with a wrong accent, since the adjective is not περίοργος [exceedingly wrathful], but περιοργής [exceedingly wrathful].
and it is lawful to desire vehemently with eagerness for virgin blood
by report of what message do you sacrifice, sent around?
which the scholiast explained by περιεσκεπασμένην [covered around].
to fall around, to be poured around
to fall around, to be poured around
where a recent hand in M has περιπιτνεῖ [it falls around], as often πιτνεῖν [to fall] for πίτνειν [to fall] in the manuscripts of the tragedians.
some cold falls around my heart
of the garments being torn all around
